acceptance_condition: Either prove N(H)>=(log H)^{1+delta} for an explicit delta>0 with constants, or prove that along all but o(depth) levels the two-child branches have average log-growth slope 3, blocking this route.
rationale: The binary-subtree argument is limited by the worst-case estimate child max<=4d^3, whose level-t height bound is 3^t A and yields only 2^t=(log H)^{log_3 2}; surpassing Theta(log H) requires typical, not worst-case, growth control.
text: Can the lower bound be pushed beyond Theta(log H)? Prove or refute that inside subtree(v2) a positive-density set of vertices has two children with average log-growth slope strictly below 3 over Omega(depth) consecutive levels, yielding N(H)>=(log H)^{1+delta} for some delta>0.
